name: GM Customer Care & Aftersales - Rancho Cucamonga Parts Distribution Center, CA

fieldNotes.identification: Confirmed via GM media/pressroom pages: GM Customer Care & Aftersales Rancho Cucamonga Parts Distribution Center, 9150 Hermosa Ave, opened 2002, ~404,000 sq ft, UAW Local 6645. Located it as the large solar-roofed tilt-up DC running E-W with its dock face and screen-walled truck yard along the south public road (6th St), confirmed in 2025 Street View. Note: an earlier Ford PDC audit in this repo reused the same building/coords; the address 9150 Hermosa is GM's facility.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Continuous concrete tilt-up screen/parapet wall rings the south truck yard along the public road (2025 Street View). Truck access is through two driveway breaks in the wall; the east driveway shows a dark sliding gate across the opening with a small marker post - controlled entry, set true.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed guard booth visible at either driveway in Street View; openings are gated but appear unmanned. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Gate present, no confirmed booth -> remote/kiosk check-in implied; set true at low confidence.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Long continuous dock-door bank runs the full south face of the building with many trailers (green/red/blue/white) backed in across the truck court; ~55 estimated -> 50+ band. Single-load building (docks on south face only).
fieldNotes.dropArea: Row of drop trailers (no tractors) parked along the inside of the south screen wall in addition to dock-staged units; ~15-20 in the parking row -> 10-25 band.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated trailer-parking row along the south frontage inside the wall, separate from the active dock apron.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Wide paved truck court between the dock face and the drop-trailer row gives inside-the-gate holding room.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Deep truck court off each driveway holds a 3+ truck queue before the docks.
fieldNotes.entryExitSeparate: Two separate driveway breaks in the south wall (west and east) serve the yard, supporting split in/out flow.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide paved truck court and two driveway aprons leave room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur into the property; dense Inland Empire warehouse district served entirely by truck.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Dense Rancho Cucamonga industrial/logistics district off arterial roads -> Urban.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~404k sq ft building plus south truck court / drop yard on a ~20-acre parcel (overhead estimate from the perimeter ring).
fieldNotes.truckGateCount: Two driveway breaks in the south screen wall.
